tei:titleStmt.tei:title: יוֹם נִלְחֲמוּ בִי
Yom Nilḥamu Vi — reshut No8 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Avraham ibn-Ezra

tei:div.tei:head: Yom Nilḥamu Vi — reshut No8 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Avraham ibn-Ezra

tei:lg.tei:l: From the day my neighbors together battled to do me harm,
the Cause’s mercies have been my arm.
Allow me to groan, like gazelles at the pool,
At the height of the giant-like hateful and cruel.
The heavenly lights’s glow turned to crepuscule,
My children’s sheaves bent, and my face in alarm
Fell, I have in my years no more charm.
From...
Bereft my children orphaned in their parents’ life,
and Deity-mockers overwhelmed them with strife,
Spilling their infants’ blood like water with their knife,
Before me on many threes they hang and they harm
And rip up mother and child with unpitying arm.
From...
Rapine came against me on countless occasions,
Honored women died from starvations,
Their children to prey for wildlife predations,
My little ones from want of bread ended in harm.
At all this, Cause, will You still not raise Your arm?
From...
Hauling the murdered ones by their feet,
They hanged them there, left them in the he heat;
Returning once-strayed daughters sweet,
Were mourning my elders who bought the farm.
Sabbath and festival the Cause did disarm!
From...
My enemies, when will I see vengeance upon them?
Gather my children from lands far beyond them
Return in repentance the cities long-gone, then
In Your house musicians and singers with sing to applause,
And bless Your name, o Cause.
In Your house...

tei:note.tei:p: Literally: “for this will You hold Yourself back.” Isaiah 64:11
In some texts, מָתַי לָאֲבֵלִים תַּשְׁמִֽיעַ נֶחָמוֹת — Mourners, when will You tell them comfort? A euphemistic rewrite.
